big: The FY27 defence allocation is ₹7.85 lakh crore, up about 15% on ₹6.81 lakh crore. But the number that matters to suppliers is not the total. It is the part that buys jets, ships and missiles: the capital outlay.

lines: ₹7.85 lakh crore. Is all of that for new weapons?
No. Much goes to pay and pensions. The capital outlay is ₹2.19 lakh crore, up about 21.8%. Within it, ₹1.85 lakh crore is for modernisation, and 75% of that is kept for domestic industry.

q: Which part of the budget buys jets, ships and missiles?
opts: Pay and allowances of all staff
Pensions of retired staff and kin
why: Pay and allowances go to serving personnel. The details here point elsewhere.
Capital outlay is the money that buys equipment. That matches the case described.
Pensions go to retired personnel. That does not match this case.
Upkeep keeps current assets running. It does not fit the facts given.

q: ₹1.39 lakh crore is what share of the ₹1.85 lakh crore modernisation budget?
why: 100% would be the whole ₹1.85 lakh crore.

q: What is the approximate rise in the FY27 allocation over ₹6.81 lakh crore?
why: 5% would give only about ₹7.15 lakh crore.
1.5% would give only about ₹6.91 lakh crore.

q: Why does a domestic reservation matter to Indian suppliers?
opts: It makes all imports illegal now
It sets their share prices daily
It directs more orders to them
It guarantees their profits each year
why: Imports remain possible outside the reserved part.
Budgets do not set share prices. It does not answer what was asked.
It reserves ₹1.39 lakh crore for domestic industry.
Orders do not guarantee profits. That does not match this case.
